_comment: The corpus for the one Hebrew name normaliser, written three times.
`fold` decides which written spellings of a sefer's name are the same sefer,
and it exists in Rust (engine/src/sefarim.rs, for the catalogue lookup), in
Typst (engine/typst/ksav.typ `_ix_fold`, for the source index) and in
TypeScript (app/src/sefarim.ts, for citation autocomplete). Three languages,
one rule, and no way to share the code: a Typst prelude cannot call Rust and
a browser tab cannot call either.
So the rule is fenced by an oracle rather than by a shared implementation.
Each case names an input and the exact string all three must fold it to; the
`class` groups the spellings that must therefore compare equal. Rust and
TypeScript check the exact strings; the Typst copy is checked on the
equivalence classes, because reading an exact string back out of a laid-out
page is a test of Typst's line breaking, not of the fold.
Edit this file, not the three implementations, when the rule changes.
cargo test --test one_want   ·   npm test
One class is here to record a thing the fold does NOT do. `fold`'s own
doc comment claimed that `ב״ב`, `ב"ב` and `ב ״ ב` all find the same
masechta. The first two do; the third does not, in any of the three
implementations — runs of whitespace collapse to one space, they do not
vanish, so `ב ״ ב` folds to `ב " ב` and `lookup` returns None. Making it
vanish is the wrong fix: a geresh ending a word is legitimately followed
by a space (`תוס׳ ד״ה` is two words), so deleting spaces around the mark
would fuse them. The comment was corrected instead, and the case is kept
as its own class so that nobody 'fixes' it back.
